relevance_note: The paper describes four patients from two families carrying heterozygous TNFAIP3 variants: "WES revealed heterozygous c.559C > T in the TNFAIP3 gene in P1, P2 and P3, while the c.259C > T mutation in the TNFAIP3 gene was identified in P4".
method_note: Read the full paper and transcribed by hand into a Python build script (scratch only); the script resolves each quote to the exact paper substring (the paper uses thin spaces in variants, ages and units) and fails if a quote is absent; table segments were checked against Tables 1-3. Labels: P1-P4 as in the text (Table 1/2 'Patient no' 1-4; Table 3 'Case 1', 'Case 2', 'Case 4'). Table 3 has patients as columns (header 'Case 1 | | Case 2 | | Case 4 |' with Pretherapy/posttherapy sub-columns); spans run from the row label through the patient's pretherapy cell or the whole row with the normal range. ESR/CRP for P2 and P4 are recorded as elevated only because the printed pretherapy values exceed the table's own normal range; other Table 3 values (IL-6, ferritin, complement, blood counts) were not turned into features unless the text states them. Table 2 'No' cells are recorded as explicit absence for that organ column; the 'Ulcers' column is read as mucocutaneous ulcers because GI findings sit in the 'Intestinal' column (so P2 'Ulcers: No' is not treated as contradicting P2's GI ulcers). 'Cardiovascular: No' is not used to exclude the composite 'pericarditis or other serositis'. Eye/skin exclusions for all four come from the explicitly named group statement ('All patients'/'Four patients all'). Unaffected relatives who tested negative (P4's parents; 'other members in family 1', i.e. the mother and grandparents implied by Fig. 3 legend and consent) are not given rows: they have no individual label or clinical description; their testing is recorded in parental_testing_statement. P4 is not called proband in the paper, so is_proband is null. Decimal ages are given as decimal-year ISO 8601 durations (e.g. P14.1Y). Age at diagnosis is not given for anyone. Variant c.559C>T was 'reported by other study [16]' - this is the variant, not the same patients, so cites_prior_report is null. No variants in other genes ('No mutations were detected in other genes associated with autoinflammatory diseases'). CONTRADICTIONS: (1) P2 onset 'at age 2.6' (text) vs '2.5 years' (Table 1); Table 1 recorded in individuals, text in feature onset. (2) P4 onset 'at the age of 7 years' (text) vs '6.9 years' (Table 1); P4 age 'a 9-year-old girl' (text) vs current age '8.3 years' (Table 1); Table 1 recorded. (3) Fig. 2 legend attributes knee synovitis (2e) and ILD (2f) to P3, but the text cites Fig. 2e/2f for P4, Table 2 gives P3 lung 'No', and P3 'refused further assessment' - probable legend mislabel; both P3 ILD rows emitted and P3 ILD checklist set to not reported; P3 synovitis row emitted from the legend as printed. (4) P4 oral ulcers (text, reason for referral) vs Table 2 Ulcers 'No'; both rows emitted, oral ulcers checklist not reported, and genital ulcers left not reported because that cell is unreliable. (5) P4 'positive ANA and anti-ds DNA antibodies' at referral vs 'no other autoantibody was detected' on admission and Table 3 anti-dsDNA '–'; both rows emitted (autoantibody checklist stays observed via ANA). (6) P1 'other autoantibodies were negative' vs Table 3 anti-dsDNA '+' pretherapy; both rows emitted. (7) P4 Table 2 Liver 'No' vs increased ALT/AST in text; autoimmune hepatitis checklist left not reported. (8) Current treatment: text for P2 (etanercept, Etiasa, MTX) and P4 (etanercept + low-dose prednisolone) lists fewer drugs than Table 1 (adds prednisolone for P2; CSA and diclofenac for P4). (9) P3 'de novo' is stated by the authors after testing 'other members in family 1', but P3's parents are not explicitly named as tested.
